newsitem.title: POLAND: WARSAW BOURSE UPS LISTING STANDARDS,DIVIDES PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: WARSAW BOURSE UPS LISTING STANDARDS,DIVIDES PROFIT.

text.p: The Warsaw Stock Exchange shareholders approved the bourse's new regulations and approved 1996 report showing a net profit of 32.8 million zlotys, Gazeta Prawa i Gospodarki said on Wednesday.
It said the new regulations increased listing requirements for companies, introduced a new institution of a market animator and allowed for derivatives trade.

The new regulations, expected to come into force in August or September, would increase capital requirements for companies seeking listing on its main and parallel markets, from seven million zlotys to 10 million zlotys and from three million zlotys to five million zlotys, respectively.
The minimum capital requirement for third floor trading is four million zlotys.

It said that bourse shareholders decided to use 90 percent of last year's profit to increase the exchange's reserve capital with the rest earmarked for a special social fund and employees' bonuses. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
